title: Cake Flour vs All-Purpose Flour: Why Texture Changes

seo.title: Cake Flour vs All-Purpose Flour
seo.meta_description: Cake flour commonly has about 7–9% protein versus roughly 10–12% in U.S. all-purpose flour. Less protein means less gluten potential and a finer, more tender crumb.
seo.search_intent: Compare cake flour and all-purpose flour by protein, gluten, and texture.

excerpt: Cake flour typically contains about 7–9% protein compared with roughly 10–12% in all-purpose flour. That lower protein level limits gluten formation and helps cakes stay fine-crumbed and tender.
content_html:
Cake flour is milled for tenderness rather than chew. It commonly contains about 7–9% protein, compared with roughly 10–12% in U.S. all-purpose flour, giving it less gluten-forming potential.

Lower protein keeps cake tender

Gluten is useful in bread but too much can make a cake rubbery or coarse. Cake flour limits how strong that network can become, which helps produce a finer, softer crumb.

Some cake flour is also treated differently

Many U.S. cake flours are finely milled and some are chlorinated, a treatment that changes starch and protein behavior. That is one reason certain classic cake formulas depend on cake flour specifically.

All-purpose flour still works in many cakes

Gentle mixing reduces gluten development. A cake made with all-purpose flour may be slightly firmer, but the difference can be small in recipes with plenty of fat and sugar.

Homemade substitutions are approximations

Replacing part of all-purpose flour with cornstarch lowers the effective protein concentration, but it does not reproduce every property of commercial cake flour.

The practical choice

Use cake flour when a very fine, tender crumb is central to the recipe; all-purpose is more versatile and works well when extreme tenderness is not required.

faq.question: Which has less protein?
faq.answer: Cake flour, usually around 7–9% versus about 10–12% for all-purpose flour.

faq.question: Can I bake cake with all-purpose flour?
faq.answer: Yes. The crumb may be slightly firmer, especially if the batter is overmixed.

faq.question: Is cornstarch plus all-purpose exactly cake flour?
faq.answer: No. It lowers the effective protein but does not reproduce every milling or treatment property.
